editorial_note: Canto 11 data remains under full source and translation review. The Sanskrit and English records are draft material tied to the pinned source; phrase coverage and all lexical choices still require chapter-by-chapter verification.

entries.sanskrit: द्वितीये निमिजायन्त-संवादेन नारदः । धर्मान् भागवतान् भक्त्या वसुदेवाय पृच्छते ॥ओ॥ अभीक्ष्णं प्रस्थापितोऽपि पुनः पुनर् अवात्सीद् इत्य् अर्थः । ननु नारदस्य दक्ष-शापान् नैकत्र-वासः सम्भवतीत्य् आशङ्क्याह---गोविन्द-भुज-गुप्तायाम् इति । न तस्यां शापादेः प्रभाव इत्य् अर्थः । कृष्णोपासने लालसा औत्कण्ठ्यं यस्य सः ॥१॥
word_for_word: by means of the dialogue between Nimi and the Jāyanteyas
the practices of the Lord's devotees
to Vasudeva, who asks with devotion
staying in one place is not possible
in the place protected by Govinda's arms
the power of curses and the like
entries.literal_english: In the second chapter Nārada [teaches] the duties of the Lord's devotees to Vasudeva, who asks with devotion, through the dialogue between Nimi and the Jāyanteyas. 'Frequently' means that, even when sent elsewhere, Nārada lived there again and again. One may object that Dakṣa's curse prevents Nārada from staying in one place; anticipating this he says 'in [Dvārakā] protected by Govinda's arms.' There the power of a curse and similar things does not operate. 'Longing for Kṛṣṇa's worship' means being filled with eager yearning for it.
entries.note: The introductory stanza has an implied verb in the rendering; the source retains its manuscript-like ॥ओ॥ marker, not silently converted into a numbered Bhāgavatam verse.

entries.sanskrit: यद्-भजने मुक्तानाम् अपीदृशम् औत्सुक्यं तं को नाम न भजेत् ? इत्य् आह---को न्व् इति । इन्द्रियवान् इति इन्द्रियवत्त्व-मात्रम् एव यत्राधिकारि-विशेषणम् इत्य् अर्थः । सर्वतः सर्वेष्व् अपि लोकेषु मृत्युर् यस्य सः ॥२॥
word_for_word: who indeed would not worship him?
is the qualification of a person eligible [to worship] in this case
one for whom there is death
entries.literal_english: Even liberated persons have such eagerness to worship him; who indeed would fail to worship him? This is the question introduced by 'who indeed?' Saying 'possessed of senses' means that merely having senses is the qualification for this worship. 'Surrounded by death' means one for whom death exists in all the worlds.
entries.note: The primary text groups verses 2–3 together but Śrīdhara's Sanskrit explains only verse 2 and ends ॥२॥. Verse 3 receives no invented gloss.

entries.sanskrit: यथा पित्रोर् यात्रा आगमनम् अपत्यानां स्वस्तये मङ्गलाय । यथा च उत्तम-श्लोकस्य वर्त्म-भूतानां महतां यात्रा कृपणानां स्वस्तये, तथा भगवद्-रूपस्य भवतो यात्रा सर्व-देहिनां स्वस्तय इति ॥४॥
word_for_word: of those who have become the way to the Lord praised in excellent verses
of one who has the form of the Lord
is for the welfare of all embodied beings
entries.literal_english: Just as a visit from parents brings welfare and auspiciousness to their children, and just as the visit of great persons who serve as the path to the Lord brings welfare to the distressed, so your arrival, for you bear the form of the Lord, brings welfare to all embodied beings.

entries.sanskrit: देवैर् अपि महताम् उपमानम् अनुचितम् इत्य् आह---भूतानाम् इति । देवानां चरितम् अतिवृष्ट्य्-आदिना भूतानां दुःखायापि भवति । त्वादृशां त्वया सदृशानाम् । अच्युते आत्मा येषां तेषाम् ॥५॥
word_for_word: through excessive rain and the like
can even cause suffering to living beings
those whose self is in Acyuta
entries.literal_english: Even comparing great souls with gods is inappropriate; this is expressed in the verse beginning 'of beings.' The gods' actions may sometimes distress creatures, as through excessively heavy rain. 'Those like you' means people resembling you, whose very self is centered in Acyuta.
entries.note: The source begins this verse directly with Śrīdhara's commentary, without a separately transcribed Bhāgavatam Sanskrit verse in this witness; the reader retains its independently mirrored verse fields.

entries.sanskrit: किं च, सुखं कुर्वन्तोऽपि देवा भजनानुसारेण कुर्वन्ति, न तथा साधव इत्य् आह---भजन्तीति । छायेव यथा पुरुषो यावत् करोति, तावद् एव तस्य छायापि, तथा कर्म-सचिवाः कर्म-सहायाः ॥६॥
word_for_word: even when the gods grant happiness
they do it in proportion to worship
just as whatever a person does
his shadow does just that much
so [the gods] are assistants of action
entries.literal_english: Moreover, even when gods bestow happiness, they do so in proportion to worship; saints do not act in that way. That is the point of the verse beginning 'they worship.' Like a person's shadow, which does only what the person does, the gods are 'assistants to action': helpers who follow action.

entries.sanskrit: तद् एवं यद्य् अपि भवत आगमन-मात्रेणैव वयं कृतार्थाः, तथापि पृच्छामः। तवेति, तव यैर् धर्मैः प्रसन्नो भगवांस् तान् इत्य् अर्थः ॥७॥
entries.literal_english: Although your arrival alone has already fulfilled our purpose, we nevertheless ask. 'Your [practices]' means those practices of yours by which the Lord becomes pleased.

entries.sanskrit: ननु त्वत्तोऽपि किम् अन्यो भगवत्-प्रसाद-पात्रम् अस्ति ? तत्राह---अहं किलेति । भुवि प्रजार्थोऽपूजयं पुत्र-लाभ-प्रयोजनः सन् पूजितवान् । किल इति सूती-गृहे भगवद्-उक्तम् अनुस्मरति (च्फ़्। १०.३.३२-४२) ॥८॥
word_for_word: a recipient of the Lord's grace
having the obtaining of a son as my objective
recalls what the Lord had said
entries.literal_english: One might ask: Is there anyone who has received the Lord's grace more than you? Vasudeva answers with the verse beginning 'indeed I.' 'I worshipped on earth for offspring' means that gaining a son was the object of his worship. 'Indeed' recalls what the Lord said in the birth chamber (see 10.3.32–42).
entries.note: The source includes the English-style cross-reference 'च्फ़्।'; it is noted rather than silently normalized into a Sanskrit reading.

entries.sanskrit: अतो यथा मुच्येमहि, तथा नोऽस्मान् शाधि शिक्षय । विचित्राणि व्यसनानि यस्मिन् संसारे, तस्मात् संसारात् । तथा विश्वतः सर्वतो भयं यस्मिंस् तस्मात् । भवद्भिर् हेतु-भूतैः । अञ्जसा अनायासेन । अद्धा साक्षात् ॥९॥
word_for_word: in whatever way we might be liberated
in the worldly cycle in which [they occur]
entries.literal_english: Therefore instruct us so that we may be freed. The world is a cycle marked by varied misfortunes, from which we seek release, and it is a place of fear on every side. Through you as the means, let this happen easily, without strain, and directly.

entries.sanskrit: हरेर् गुणैर् वर्णनीयत्वेन प्रस्तुतैर् हरिः संस्मारित इत्य् अर्थः ॥१०॥
word_for_word: presented as subjects to be described
entries.literal_english: Hari was brought to mind by his qualities, introduced as subjects for description.

scope: Complete source-bound Śrīdhara commentary for Canto 11 Chapter 2, verses 11.2.1–11.2.10; 11.2.3 has no separate commentary and is handled by the reader sentinel.
